nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a variable context, $S$ a store typing and $\mu$ a store that is well typed under $\Gamma$ and $S$. If $v$ is a value of type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$, then the store obtained by appending $v$ at the end of $\mu$ is well typed under $\Gamma$ and the store typing obtained by appending $T$ at the end of $S$.
nodes.title: Allocation preserves store typing

nodes.summary: The term $b_0 = \lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ (!\ell_0)\,x$, which applies the contents of store location $\ell_0 = 0$ to its argument.
nodes.title: The stored recursive function of Landin's knot

nodes.summary: The term $\lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ (!r)\,x$, which applies the contents of the reference $r$ to its argument. Here $r$ is a free variable, de Bruijn index $1$ under the binder $\lambda x$; in Landin's knot it is bound by the outer $\lambda r$.
nodes.title: The recursive function of Landin's knot, with the cell free

nodes.summary: The term $(\lambda r{:}\mathrm{Ref}\,(\mathrm{Unit}\to\mathrm{Unit}).\ (\lambda y{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ (!r)\, \mathrm{unit})\ (r := \lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ (!r)\,x))\ \ell_0$, where $\ell_0$ is store location $0$: Landin's knot with its allocation $\mathrm{ref}\,(\lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ x)$ replaced by $\ell_0$.
nodes.title: The knot after allocation

nodes.summary: If a configuration $(t, \mu)$ steps to $(t_1, \mu_1)$ and also to $(t_2, \mu_2)$, then $t_1 = t_2$ and $\mu_1 = \mu_2$.
nodes.title: Determinism of evaluation with references

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $S$ a store typing, and $\mu$ a store (a list of terms, whose entry at index $l$ is the contents of location $l$) that is well typed, $\Gamma \mid S \vdash \mu$. If $S$ assigns type $T$ to location $l$, then $\mu$ has an entry $v$ at location $l$, $v$ is a value, and $\Gamma \mid S \vdash v : T$.
nodes.title: Well-typed stores hold a typed value at every location

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a variable context, let $S$ and $S'$ be store typings such that $S$ is a prefix of $S'$, and let $\mu$ be a store that is well typed under $\Gamma$ and $S$. Then $\mu$ and $S$ have the same length, and for every location $l$ less than this length, the entry of $\mu$ at $l$ is a value that has, under $\Gamma$ and $S'$, the type that $S$ assigns to $l$.
nodes.title: Retyping a well-typed store under an extended store typing

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a variable context and let $S$ and $S'$ be store typings such that $S$ is a prefix of $S'$. If a term $t$ has type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$, then $t$ has type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S'$.
nodes.title: Store-typing weakening

nodes.summary: The judgment $\Gamma \mid S \vdash t : T$ (TAPL Figure 13-1), where the context $\Gamma$ lists the types of the free de Bruijn variables (index $0$ first) and the store typing $S$ lists the types of the locations $0, 1, \ldots$, is the least relation closed under the following rules, in which $t : T$ abbreviates $\Gamma \mid S \vdash t : T$. A variable $x$ has type $T$ if $\Gamma$ assigns $T$ to index $x$. If $t$…
nodes.title: Typing judgment for the lambda calculus with references

nodes.summary: The identity function $\lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ x$ on the unit type.
nodes.title: The identity on Unit

nodes.summary: For terms $t$ and $s$, the instantiation of $t$ by $s$ applies to $t$ the parallel substitution that sends the de Bruijn index $0$ to $s$ and each index $x + 1$ to the variable $x$. Thus the free occurrences of variable $0$ in $t$ are replaced by $s$, with the free variables of $s$ raised by the number of binders crossed, and every other free variable of $t$ is lowered by one.
nodes.title: Substitution of a term for variable zero

nodes.summary: For all terms $t$ and $s$ of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, shift every free de Bruijn variable of $t$ up by one (rename by $x \mapsto x + 1$), then instantiate the result with $s$, replacing variable $0$ by $s$ and lowering every other variable $x + 1$ to $x$. The outcome is $t$.
nodes.title: Instantiating a shifted term

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a variable context and $S$ a store typing. If a term $t$ has type $T$ under $S$ and the context that extends $\Gamma$ by a new innermost variable (index $0$) of type $A$, and a term $s$ has type $A$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$, then substituting $s$ for variable $0$ in $t$ (and lowering every other variable by one) gives a term of type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$.
nodes.title: Substitution lemma for the lambda calculus with references

nodes.summary: Write $\ell_0$ for store location $0$, let $b_0 = \lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ (!\ell_0)\,x$, and let $[b_0]$ be the store whose only entry, at $\ell_0$, is $b_0$. In one call-by-value step, $(!\ell_0)\,\mathrm{unit}$ with store $[b_0]$ steps to $b_0\,\mathrm{unit}$ with store $[b_0]$, and in one further step $b_0\,\mathrm{unit}$ with store $[b_0]$ steps back to $(!\ell_0)\,\mathrm{unit}$ with store $[b_0]$.
nodes.title: The cycle of Landin's knot

nodes.summary: Starting from Landin's knot with the empty store, no sequence of zero or more call-by-value evaluation steps reaches a configuration $(v, \mu)$ in which the term $v$ is a value, whatever the store $\mu$.
nodes.title: Landin's knot never evaluates to a value

nodes.summary: Landin's knot is closed and has type $\mathrm{Unit}$ in the empty typing context under the empty store typing.
nodes.title: Landin's knot is well typed

nodes.summary: Write $\ell_0$ for store location $0$ and $[t]$ for the store whose only entry, at $\ell_0$, is $t$, and let $\mathrm{id} = \lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ x$ and $b_0 = \lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\ (!\ell_0)\,x$. Each of the following is one call-by-value step: Landin's knot with the empty store steps to…
nodes.title: The first four steps of Landin's knot

nodes.summary: If Landin's knot with the empty store evaluates in zero or more call-by-value steps to a term $t$ with store $\mu$, then $t$ with store $\mu$ takes a further step to some term $t'$ with some store $\mu'$. So the evaluation of the knot runs forever.
nodes.title: Landin's knot never gets stuck

nodes.summary: The term
nodes.title: Landin's knot

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$ and store typing $S$, if $v$ is a value and $\Gamma \mid S \vdash v : T_1 \to T_2$, then $v$ is an abstraction $\lambda{:}T_1.\, t$ with parameter type $T_1$, for some body $t$.
nodes.title: Canonical forms for function types

nodes.summary: Given a renaming $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of de Bruijn indices, its lift is the renaming that sends $0$ to $0$ and each $x + 1$ to $\rho(x) + 1$.
nodes.title: Lifting a renaming under a binder in the lambda calculus with references

nodes.summary: Given a substitution $\sigma$ assigning a term to each de Bruijn index, its lift is the substitution that sends $0$ to the variable $0$ and each $x + 1$ to the term $\sigma(x)$ renamed by $n \mapsto n + 1$, that is, with every free variable raised by one.
nodes.title: Lifting a substitution under a binder

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$ and store typing $S$, if $v$ is a value and $\Gamma \mid S \vdash v : \mathrm{Ref}\, T$, then $v$ is a location $l$ to which $S$ assigns type $T$.
nodes.title: Canonical forms for reference types

nodes.summary: The term $(!\ell_0)\ \mathrm{unit}$: the dereference of the store location $\ell_0$ (location $0$), applied to the unit value.
nodes.title: Cycle term of Landin's knot

nodes.summary: If $v$ is a value, then there are no stores $\mu$, $\mu'$ and term $t'$ such that the configuration $(v, \mu)$ steps to $(t', \mu')$: values are normal forms.
nodes.title: Values do not step

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$, store typing $S$ and base type $b$, there is no value $v$ with $\Gamma \mid S \vdash v : b$.
nodes.title: No value has a base type

nodes.summary: Fix a type $B$ of base types, and write $\iota$ for the embeddings of simple types and of raw terms of the simply typed lambda calculus over $B$ into types and terms of the calculus with references over $B$. Let $\Gamma$ be a context of simple types, $t$ a raw term and $A$ a simple type such that $t$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$. Then for every store typing $S$ we have $\iota(\Gamma) \mid S \vdash \iota(t) : \iota(A)$,…
nodes.title: Typing is preserved by the embedding of raw STLC terms

nodes.summary: Fix a type $B$ of base types. The embedding $\iota$ sends a raw (extrinsically typed, binder-annotated) term of the simply typed lambda calculus over $B$ to a term of the calculus with references over $B$, by recursion: a de Bruijn variable $n$ goes to the variable $n$, an application $f\,a$ goes to $\iota(f)\,\iota(a)$, and an abstraction $\lambda{:}A.\,t$ goes to $\lambda{:}\iota(A).\,\iota(t)$, where $\iota(A)$…
nodes.title: Embedding of raw STLC terms into the calculus with references

nodes.summary: Fix a type $B$ of base types, and write $\iota$ for the embeddings of simple types and of raw terms of the simply typed lambda calculus over $B$ into types and terms of the calculus with references over $B$. Let $\Gamma$ be a context of simple types, $A$ a simple type and $t$ an intrinsically typed term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, and let $\mathrm{erase}(t)$ be the raw term obtained from $t$ by erasing its typing…
nodes.title: Typing of embedded intrinsically typed STLC terms

nodes.summary: Fix a type $B$ of base types. The embedding $\iota$ sends a simple type over $B$ to a type of the calculus with references over $B$, by recursion: $\iota(b) = b$ for a base type $b \in B$, and $\iota(A_1 \to A_2) = \iota(A_1) \to \iota(A_2)$.
nodes.title: Embedding of simple types into the calculus with references

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a variable context and $S$ a store typing. If a term $t$ has type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$, the store $\mu$ is well typed under $\Gamma$ and $S$, and $t$ with store $\mu$ evaluates in zero or more steps to $t'$ with store $\mu'$, then there is a store typing $S'$ having $S$ as a prefix such that $t'$ has type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S'$ and $\mu'$ is well typed under $\Gamma$ and $S'$.
nodes.title: Preservation for multi-step evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a variable context and $S$ a store typing. If a term $t$ has type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$, the store $\mu$ is well typed under $\Gamma$ and $S$, and $t$ with store $\mu$ takes one evaluation step to $t'$ with store $\mu'$, then there is a store typing $S'$ having $S$ as a prefix such that $t'$ has type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S'$ and $\mu'$ is well typed under $\Gamma$ and $S'$.
nodes.title: Preservation for the lambda calculus with references

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a store typing, $t$ a term of some type $T$ in the empty variable context under $S$, and $\mu$ a store that is well typed under $S$ in the empty context. Then $t$ is a value, or the configuration $(t, \mu)$ takes an evaluation step to some $(t', \mu')$.
nodes.title: Progress

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be Landin's knot, $\iota = \lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\,x$, $b_0 = \lambda x{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\,(!\ell_0)\,x$ with $\ell_0$ the store location $0$, $a = (!\ell_0)\ \mathrm{unit}$, $b = b_0\ \mathrm{unit}$, $c_1$ the term $K$ with its argument $\mathrm{ref}\ \iota$ replaced by $\ell_0$, $c_2 = (\lambda y{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\,a)\,(\ell_0 := b_0)$ and $c_3 = (\lambda y{:}\mathrm{Unit}.\,a)\ \mathrm{unit}$; write…
nodes.title: Configurations on the evaluation path of Landin's knot

nodes.summary: Given a renaming $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of de Bruijn indices, renaming a term by $\rho$ replaces each variable $x$ by $\rho(x)$; renames the body of an abstraction $\lambda{:}T.\,t$ by the lift of $\rho$ (which sends $0$ to $0$ and each $x + 1$ to $\rho(x) + 1$), keeping the type annotation $T$; leaves the unit value and store locations unchanged; and acts componentwise on applications, allocations,…
nodes.title: Renaming the variables of a term

nodes.summary: Let $\rho, \rho' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be renamings of de Bruijn variables with $\rho(x) = \rho'(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{N}$. Then for every term $t$ of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, renaming $t$ by $\rho$ gives the same term as renaming $t$ by $\rho'$.
nodes.title: Renaming respects pointwise equality

nodes.summary: For every term $t$ of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, renaming the de Bruijn variables of $t$ by the identity map of $\mathbb{N}$ gives back $t$.
nodes.title: Renaming by the identity

nodes.summary: For all renamings $\rho, \rho' : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of de Bruijn variables and every term $t$ of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, renaming $t$ by $\rho$ and then renaming the result by $\rho'$ gives the same term as renaming $t$ by the composite $\rho' \circ \rho$.
nodes.title: Composition of renamings

nodes.summary: Let $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a renaming of de Bruijn variables, $\sigma$ a parallel substitution sending each index to a term of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, and $t$ a term. Applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and then renaming the result by $\rho$ gives the same term as applying to $t$ the substitution that sends each index $x$ to the renaming of $\sigma(x)$ by $\rho$.
nodes.title: Substituting then renaming

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be variable contexts, $S$ a store typing, and $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ a renaming of variable indices such that whenever $\Gamma$ assigns type $A$ to variable $x$, $\Delta$ assigns type $A$ to variable $\rho(x)$. If a term $t$ has type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$, then the term obtained from $t$ by renaming its variables by $\rho$ has type $T$ under $\Delta$ and $S$.
nodes.title: Renaming preserves typing

nodes.summary: Let the store $\mu$ be well typed under the variable context $\Gamma$ and the store typing $S$, and let $l$ be a location to which $S$ assigns the type $T$. If $v$ is a value of type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$, then the store obtained from $\mu$ by overwriting the entry at $l$ with $v$ is well typed under $\Gamma$ and $S$.
nodes.title: Assignment preserves store typing

nodes.summary: For a term $s$, the single-variable substitution for $s$ sends the de Bruijn index $0$ to $s$ and each index $x + 1$ to the variable $x$.
nodes.title: Single-variable substitution at index zero

nodes.summary: One step of call-by-value evaluation $t \mid \mu \to t' \mid \mu'$, from a term $t$ with a store $\mu$ to a term $t'$ with a store $\mu'$, is the least relation closed under the following rules, in which $v$, $v_1$ and $v_2$ are values. If $t \mid \mu \to t' \mid \mu'$, then $t\,t_2 \mid \mu \to t'\,t_2 \mid \mu'$, $v_1\,t \mid \mu \to v_1\,t' \mid \mu'$, $\mathsf{ref}\,t \mid \mu \to \mathsf{ref}\,t' \mid \mu'$,…
nodes.title: One-step evaluation with references

nodes.summary: The relation $t \mid \mu \to^* t' \mid \mu'$ holds when the configuration $(t, \mu)$ reaches $(t', \mu')$ in zero or more evaluation steps; that is, it is the reflexive-transitive closure of one-step evaluation on pairs of a term and a store.
nodes.title: Multi-step evaluation with references

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a variable context and $S$ a store typing. A store $\mu$, a list of terms whose entry at index $l$ is the contents of location $l$, is well typed under $\Gamma$ and $S$, written $\Gamma \mid S \vdash \mu$, when $\mu$ and $S$ have the same length and, for every location $l$ less than this length, the entry of $\mu$ at $l$ is a value that has, under $\Gamma$ and $S$, the type that $S$ assigns to $l$.
nodes.title: Well-typed stores

nodes.summary: A store $\mu$ is a finite list of terms; each location $l$ less than the length of $\mu$ holds the term $\mu[l]$, the entry of $\mu$ at index $l$.
nodes.title: Store

nodes.summary: Given a substitution $\sigma$ assigning a term to each de Bruijn index, substituting $\sigma$ into a term replaces each variable $x$ by $\sigma(x)$; substitutes into the body of an abstraction $\lambda{:}T.\,t$ the lift of $\sigma$ (which sends $0$ to the variable $0$ and each $x + 1$ to $\sigma(x)$ with every free variable raised by one), keeping the type annotation $T$; leaves the unit value and store locations…
nodes.title: Parallel substitution in a term

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma, \sigma'$ be parallel substitutions, each sending every de Bruijn index to a term of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, with $\sigma(x) = \sigma'(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{N}$. Then for every term $t$, applying $\sigma$ to $t$ gives the same term as applying $\sigma'$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Substitution respects pointwise equality

nodes.summary: For every term $t$ of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, applying the parallel substitution that sends each de Bruijn index $x$ to the variable term $x$ gives back $t$.
nodes.title: Substitution by variables is the identity

nodes.summary: Let $\rho : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a renaming of de Bruijn variables, $\sigma$ a parallel substitution sending each index to a term of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, and $t$ a term. Renaming $t$ by $\rho$ and then applying $\sigma$ gives the same term as applying the substitution $\sigma \circ \rho$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Renaming then substituting

nodes.summary: For all parallel substitutions $\sigma, \tau$, each sending every de Bruijn index to a term of the simply typed lambda calculus with references, and every term $t$, applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and then $\tau$ to the result gives the same term as applying to $t$ the substitution that sends each index $x$ to the result of applying $\tau$ to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.title: Composition of substitutions in the lambda calculus with references

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be variable contexts, $S$ a store typing, and $\sigma$ a substitution sending each variable index to a term, such that whenever $\Gamma$ assigns type $A$ to variable $x$, the term $\sigma(x)$ has type $A$ under $\Delta$ and $S$. If a term $t$ has type $T$ under $\Gamma$ and $S$, then the term obtained from $t$ by applying $\sigma$ has type $T$ under $\Delta$ and $S$.
nodes.title: Parallel substitution preserves typing

nodes.summary: Fix a type $B$ of base types. The terms are generated by: variables, given as de Bruijn indices $x \in \mathbb{N}$; abstractions $\lambda{:}T.\,t$, where $T$ is a type over $B$ and $t$ is a term in which index $0$ refers to the abstraction's parameter; applications $t_1\,t_2$; the unit value $\mathsf{unit}$; store locations $l \in \mathbb{N}$; allocations $\mathsf{ref}\,t$; dereferences $!t$; and assignments…
nodes.title: Terms of the simply typed lambda calculus with references

nodes.summary: Fix a type $B$ of base types. The types over $B$ are generated by the grammar $T ::= b \mid \mathsf{Unit} \mid T_1 \to T_2 \mid \mathsf{Ref}\,T$ with $b \in B$: base types, the unit type, function types, and types $\mathsf{Ref}\,T$ of reference cells holding values of type $T$.
nodes.title: Types of the simply typed lambda calculus with references

nodes.summary: A closed term typed under the empty store typing, run from the empty store, never gets stuck: every term it reaches in zero or more steps, together with the store reached alongside it, is a value or can take a further step.
nodes.title: Type safety from the empty store

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a store typing, $T$ a type, $t$ a term of type $T$ in the empty variable context under $S$, and $\mu$ a store that is well typed under $S$ in the empty context. If the configuration $(t, \mu)$ evaluates in zero or more steps to $(t', \mu')$, then $t'$ is a value or $(t', \mu')$ takes a step to some configuration $(t'', \mu'')$. So a closed term that is well typed in a well-typed store never reaches a…
nodes.title: Type safety

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$ and store typing $S$, if $v$ is a value and $\Gamma \mid S \vdash v : \mathrm{Unit}$, then $v = \mathtt{unit}$.
nodes.title: Canonical forms for the unit type

nodes.summary: A term is a value if and only if it is an abstraction $\lambda{:}T.\,t$, the unit value $\mathsf{unit}$, or a store location $l$.
nodes.title: Values of the simply typed lambda calculus with references

nodes.summary: If a term $t$ has type $T$ in a variable context $\Gamma$ under a store typing $S$, then for every type $A$, the term obtained from $t$ by shifting each free de Bruijn variable up by one has type $T$ under $S$ in the context obtained from $\Gamma$ by adding $A$ in front as variable $0$.
nodes.title: Weakening of typing

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
